core.title: Pick a feature name's verb to fit its artifact type
core.given: A feature name is being authored or renamed and is seeded from an artifact whose type is event, state, data or config.
core.when: The planner picks the leading verb of the feature's verb-object slug.
core.then: Choose a leading verb appropriate to the seeding artifact's type; the by-type verbs below are suggestions, not the only legal choices.
prefer: Event: publish, emit, start, close, trigger, notify.
State: track, monitor, maintain, update, manage.
Data: create, manage, process, handle, make, generate.
Config: configure, setup, initialize, define, establish.
avoid: Treating the by-type table as the full set of legal verbs: alone it rejects even this convention's own examples.

A leading verb outside the union of the by-type suggestion verbs (verbs_by_type) and the verb-object enforcement allowlist (additional_verbs, given in full under verification); the verb-object naming gates reject it.
core.why: The artifact type (event, state, data, config) determines the appropriate verbs for the feature name, so names read consistently with what the artifact is.
evidence: A reviewer confirms the feature's leading verb is appropriate to the seeding artifact's type (the by-type table is the reference set of suggestions).
Separately (lexicon gate): the feature or product capability slug's leading token is a member of the union of the by-type suggestion verbs and the enforcement allowlist.
verification: Advisory, review-level check only: appropriateness of the leading verb to the seeding artifact's type is confirmed by review (LLM-judged from the artifact's type), with the by-type suggestion table in prefer as the reference set; 'manage' is suggested for both state and data. The table is a suggestion set, not an enforcement basis — alone it rejects even this convention's own examples.

Enforcement of leading-verb legality is a separate, unconditional lexicon gate that covers every feature and product capability slug, with or without a typed seed: a slug is accepted iff its leading token is in the union of the by-type suggestion verbs and the verb-object enforcement allowlist. There is no prerequisite that a type-appropriate verb be tried first, and this rule neither adds verbs to nor removes verbs from that gate.

The verb-object enforcement allowlist (additional_verbs) — the explicit allowlist of leading verbs a planner artifact slug may use, beyond the by-type suggestion verbs. Complete list: admit, aggregate, allocate, annotate, apply, archive, assign, attach, authenticate, author, bind, bootstrap, bridge, broadcast, build, calculate, cancel, capture, check, classify, collect, commit, compare, compose, compute, connect, consolidate, convert, copy, correct, count, credit, decode, decommission, delegate, deliver, deploy, derive, describe, detach, detect, disable, discover, dispatch, download, drive, elicit, enable, encode, enforce, enrich, ensure, escalate, estimate, evaluate, expire, export, expose, extract, fetch, filter, finalize, fix, flush, forward, freeze, gather, govern, guard, hydrate, implement, import, index, inject, inspect, integrate, invoke, isolate, judge, launch, link, lint, list, load, lock, log, map, mark, match, measure, mediate, merge, migrate, mint, normalize, observe, open, orchestrate, parse, partition, pause, persist, ping, place, plan, poll, populate, post, prepare, preview, prioritize, produce, project, promote, prompt, propagate, provision, prune, pull, purge, push, queue, rank, read, rebuild, reconcile, record, redirect, refine, refresh, register, reject, release, reload, remove, rename, render, replay, replicate, report, request, resolve, respond, restore, resume, retrieve, retry, review, revoke, rollback, route, run, sample, save, scaffold, scan, schedule, score, search, seed, select, send, serve, show, sign, simulate, snapshot, spawn, split, stop, store, stream, submit, subscribe, summarize, surface, suspend, swap, sync, tag, teardown, throttle, toggle, trace, transform, translate, trim, tune, unlock, unsubscribe, upgrade, upload, validate, verify, visualize, warn, watch, wire, wrap. This lexicon is stack-neutral, method-level naming data shared by every stack: a realization of the lexicon gate must enforce the union of this allowlist and the by-type suggestion verbs, never the by-type table alone, and this rule neither adds verbs to nor removes verbs from the union.

values: feature name slug added or renamed

fires: Planner names a new feature seeded from an event artifact such as x:started and picks the leading verb.
Planner seeds a feature name from a config, state or data artifact.
Planner renames a feature slug seeded from a typed artifact so that its leading verb changes.
doesNotFire: Naming or renaming a product capability (only the separate leading-verb lexicon gate applies).
Naming a feature that is not seeded from a typed artifact (only the separate leading-verb lexicon gate applies).
Editing a feature's acceptances or description without touching its name slug.
Coder implementing code inside an already-named feature.

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete artifact kind(s) that play the plan-artifact role in this stack — i.e. what the stack calls the planner feature artifact whose feature names this rule governs.

bunOnly.text: planner.feature.name-is-verb-object and planner.capability.name-is-verb-object accept a slug iff its leading token is in the union of additional_verbs and verbs_by_type. There is no prerequisite that a type verb be tried first. The verbs_by_type suggestion table alone is insufficient as an enforcement basis — it rejects even the convention's own examples (#1276).

neutralityNotes: This convention is method-level (planner naming of artifact-seeded feature names) and was already free of stack references, so the core keeps it essentially verbatim — no stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, file suffix or path is named. The verb lexicons are convention/method data, not stack structure: the by-type suggestion table is this rule's own content (core:prefer[0..3]) and the complete verb-object enforcement allowlist is retained in core:verification as shared stack-neutral rule data, so any realization of the unconditional union-membership gate has both operands of the union; bun.json itself proposes to split that gate into planner.artifact-naming.leading-verb-lexicon, but until such a neutral lexicon-gate rule exists this core carries the allowlist (and no profile key is proposed for it, since rule-specific permitted verbs are not structure). The Bun-specific remainder is small: sibling gate rule ids and the repository ticket #1276, sidecar-internal pointers, and the worked URN->slug examples — which stay in the delivered Bun sidecar, the reference example for other stacks. The only profile touchpoint is mapping 'planner feature artifact' to the stack's concrete plan-artifact kind via roles.plan_artifact.kinds.
